questions.q: What should you check first in the Execution Log when verifying a run of Contractor Offboarding?
options: Whether the manager's approval email used the correct font
Whether the flow's name was spelled correctly
Whether the IT task was closed before the flow ran
Whether the scheduled trigger's query actually returned the contractor record you expected
questions.explain: Verification works link by link, starting with whether the trigger's query found the right record — the same order used to diagnose a failure.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what are the four questions real process documentation should answer?
options: What color the flow's icon is, who built it, how many nodes it has, and its creation date
What triggers it, what it does step by step, who's involved, and what to check if it fails
Only the trigger type and nothing else
A full screenshot-by-screenshot walkthrough of the Flow Designer canvas
questions.explain: Those four short answers are what a future admin would actually need to support or troubleshoot the flow, per this lesson.

questions.q: Why does this lesson recommend writing process documentation at build time rather than after something breaks?
options: ServiceNow deletes flow configuration after 30 days unless documentation exists
Documentation written later is always more detailed
Build-time documentation is required before a flow can be activated
Documentation written while the design decisions are still fresh is far more accurate than documentation reconstructed later
questions.explain: Flows that depend on multiple stakeholders and external systems tend to break quietly weeks later, when the original reasoning is easy to forget.

questions.q: In the diagnostic order this lesson describes, what comes right after checking whether the trigger's query found the correct record?
options: Whether the course outline needs to be updated
Whether the If/Else branch went down the correct path, followed by whether the subflow reported a success or failure status
Whether the contractor table needs a new field added
Whether the flow should be rebuilt as a subflow instead
questions.explain: The verification walks the chain in build order: trigger, branch, subflow status, approval, then the task record.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe the relationship between Flow Designer and the course that follows it, JavaScript for ServiceNow Developers?
options: JavaScript for ServiceNow Developers replaces Flow Designer entirely and makes it obsolete
The two courses cover unrelated, non-overlapping skill sets
Flow Designer requires JavaScript knowledge as a prerequisite to use at all
Flow Designer is a low-code bridge — every mechanism it uses (trigger, branch, subflow, approval) is a visual wrapper around logic a script could also express directly
questions.explain: The course's own description frames Flow Designer as the admin-facing bridge toward the scripted development taught next.
